svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Mockup 18: the next event and the installed hub
svg.text: 18 · The next event: an installed hub belongs to one hostname, and each event has its own (Q D4)
Today: one hostname per event
demo.example.org is event 1; the next event in the series gets
its own hostname (tenants.md, Hostnames).
A PWA, its push permission and its subscription belong to one
origin. At archive Notify deletes the subscriptions.
A · A new install per event (as the contracts are)
The next event's QR and link lead to a new hostname: install
again, allow alerts again.
Simple, no change. The old icon stays on the home screen and
shows 'This event has ended'.
Cost: none. Friction every event for regulars.
B · A series hostname that moves (recommended)
The series gets a lasting hostname (series.example.org). At
clone the superadmin moves it from the old event to the new
one.
The installed app and its permission stay; on first open in
the new event the hub re-subscribes silently and asks only for
new topics.
Cost: a tenants rule for moving a hostname within a series
(additive), and the hub's re-subscribe.
C · One hub on the platform domain
hub.example.org with an event picker; tenant from the path,
not the hostname.
Breaks the tenancy rule 'the tenant comes from the hostname'
and host-only cookies (0013, #52).
Cost: L, and high risk.
Between events
Nobody can be alerted that 'the next event is live': the old subscriptions are gone (tenants.md, archive).
With B, the archived event's 'Thanks for coming' page can offer 'Remind me when the next event opens', a new opt-in that lives with the
series, not the event (Q D4, personal data: high).

Q D4 decides A, B or C. The pack recommends B: regulars come to several events a year at one venue (0022), and asking them to install and allow alerts again each time throws away the hub's best feature.
